name: Jindal Stainless Ltd
title: Jindal Stainless Ltd - 532508 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Jindal Stainless guides FY27 volume +7-9% and H1 EBITDA/ton of INR18,000-20,000 despite gas cost spiking 2.5-3x; Indonesia melt shop (1.2 Mt) adds capacity while Maharashtra capex is still in land acquisition.

summary.headline: Jindal Stainless Q4FY26 consolidated EBITDA rose 37% YoY to INR1,455 crore; FY27 volume guided at 7-9% with EBITDA/ton of INR18,000-20,000 for H1 only.
summary.overview: Q4FY26 deliveries were 0.64 million tons, flat YoY, while consolidated EBITDA rose about 37% YoY and 3% QoQ to INR1,455 crore and PAT rose about 41% YoY to INR834 crore. For FY26, volumes grew 8% to 2.57 million tons, EBITDA rose 19% to INR5,560 crore and PAT rose 27% to INR3,185 crore. Net debt fell to INR3,040 crore (0.55x net debt/EBITDA). Management flagged a sharp, sudden rise in gas and utility costs from the Middle East conflict (up around 2.5x-3x), a temporary QCO suspension, and CBAM uncertainty, and gave FY27 volume guidance but EBITDA/ton guidance only until H1.

financial_highlights.change: reduced further; net debt/EBITDA 0.55x, net debt/equity 0.15

financial_highlights.value: INR1 interim + INR3 final per share (face value INR2), ~INR330 crore total

segments.name: Stainless steel (India and Indonesia)
segments.commentary: Consolidated, with EBITDA/ton guidance covering the whole stainless business including Indonesia and Rathi. Domestic share about 92%, export share 8% of FY26 sales.

segments.name: RKEF nickel (Indonesia)
segments.commentary: Management said recent EBITDA has been around $3,000/ton of nickel versus a prior guided range of $500-1,500/ton, but flagged it is volatile and tied to Indonesian ore pricing formulas.

segments.name: Rathi (rebar subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Operated at about 80-85% utilisation in FY26; stainless rebar was about 25% of Q4 volume. Company stated Rathi is EBITDA positive, with no separate figures given.

segments.name: Jindal Stainless Steelway (fabrication subsidiary)
segments.commentary: First fabrication facility in Patalganga started operations, initial investment about INR125 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume growth guided at 7-9% (management also said 'at least 8-10%' early in the call, later clarified as 7-9%).
FY27 EBITDA/ton guidance of INR18,000-20,000 for H1 FY27 only; to be reviewed after six months depending on the situation.
FY27 capex guidance around INR2,600 crore; FY28 capex to be given later.
Sales volume target of 3.5 million tons per annum by FY29, described as double-digit CAGR over three years.
CRAP capacity to reach 2.67 million tons per annum by FY28, including the 0.17 mtpa CRAP line at Jajpur and additional INR900 crore for cold rolling at Hisar and Kharagpur.
Indonesia melt shop (1.2 mtpa) ramp-up expected to reach 70-80% of capacity during FY27.
capex_capacity: Indonesia 1.2 mtpa stainless melt shop commissioned ahead of schedule; total melting capacity now 4.2 mtpa, of which 3 mtpa in India.
Jajpur 1.1 mtpa HRAP line upcoming commissioning; 0.17 mtpa CRAP line also at Jajpur.
Additional INR900 crore to augment cold rolling at Hisar and Kharagpur.
Maharashtra greenfield: land acquisition under way, most of this year expected to go into land acquisition; downstream to be built first, then upstream. Clear plan needs a few more months.
Partial commissioning of a 315 MW solar/wind hybrid project with Oyster Renewable Energy in Q4.
demand_pricing: Domestic demand cited as resilient across automotive, ornamental and industrial pipe and tube, railway, metro, lift and elevator, and white goods; metro and passenger coach demand strong, with stainless demand expected to rise 2-3x over 3-4 years.
Export volumes rose QoQ in Q4 despite subdued global trade; focus on Japan, Korea, Taiwan and Germany; Americas remain key.

Management said cost increases were only partly passed on to customers, depending on the product and competitor pricing; imports from competitors without the same cost increases were cited as a constraint.
Gas and utility costs (propane, LPG, natural gas, ammonia, acid) rose about 2.5-3x. Management declined to quantify gas consumption.
QCO suspended for six months; management said this encourages substandard imports and dampens MSME capacity plans. Antidumping verifiers to be appointed in Q1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Can volume and EBITDA/ton guidance be given for FY27 given Middle East headwinds?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 volume growth of 7-9% and EBITDA/ton of INR18,000-20,000 for H1, with a review after six months; availability of gas is no longer the constraint in May, but cost is much higher.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the export share falling, and what is the FY27 export outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 exports were 8% of sales versus 9% in FY25. Management expects to hold 8-10% of exports in the FY27 volume growth, with disruption from the war and CBAM.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Maharashtra capex and the FY27/FY28 capex number?
qa_highlights.answer: Land acquisition is under way; FY27 capex guidance is about INR2,600 crore; FY28 figure deferred.

qa_highlights.question: How should RKEF and Indonesia be valued and treated in EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: RKEF EBITDA recently around $3,000/ton of nickel versus the earlier $500-1,500 range. The slabs are planned to be brought to India; Indonesia is a line-by-line consolidated subsidiary with minority share shown separately. Indonesia is included in the INR18,000-20,000 guidance.

qa_highlights.question: What are the mitigation plans for gas shortages?
qa_highlights.answer: Jajpur has started using natural gas for part of its needs and plans to scale up; coal gasification/syngas and green hydrogen (600 mm cube plant at Jajpur, running June-July) are being pursued; Hisar and Ghaziabad are also being worked on.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 400 series share falling, and does it affect EBITDA/ton?
qa_highlights.answer: 400 series was 18% in FY26 versus 17% in FY25, with Q4 at 19-20%. Management said it is pursuing 400 series growth and only adds volumes that improve EBITDA/ton.

risks_watch: Gas and utility cost inflation from the West Asia conflict; H1 EBITDA/ton guidance may be revised at H1.
QCO suspension for six months and imports of substandard material; antidumping process timeline.
Indonesian nickel and mining policy changes; RKEF EBITDA volatile with nickel prices.
CBAM implementation in the EU; verifiers yet to be appointed.
Ramp-up of Indonesia melt shop and balancing of slab imports against Jajpur HRAP/CRAP timing.
Declining share of 400 series relative to FY25 levels in FY26 mix (headline 17% to 18%, Q4 at 19-20%).
summary.management_tone: Confident on volume and cost recovery but openly cautious on H1 FY27 EBITDA/ton, with guidance kept only for six months due to sharp, sudden cost increases. Management was evasive on specifics: gas volumes, FY28 capex, RKEF normalised EBITDA, and defence products, and deferred several answers to follow-up calls.
key_quotes: And depending on the situation, maybe after 6 months we might revise this figure also.
So we are confident of balancing our needs as the market demands.
Now we see that life cycle cost is -- normally, people are considering life cycle cost for making a decision while choosing a product.
So, FY27 guidance, volume guidance, we have already provided, which is 7% to 9%, and that takes care of all these uncertainties.

adds.what: 1.2 mtpa stainless steel melt shop in Indonesia (commissioned, ramp-up to 70-80% during FY27)
Cold rolling augmentation at Hisar and Kharagpur (INR900 crore commitment)
First Jindal Stainless Steelway fabrication facility, Patalganga (operations started)

growth.why: FY27 volume guided at 7-9% (midpoint 8%) with Indonesia 1.2 mtpa melt shop already commissioned and ramping to 70-80% in FY27, plus a 1.1 mtpa Jajpur HRAP line and INR900 crore cold-rolling augmentation; EBITDA/ton guided only at INR18,000-20,000 for H1 FY27, and a Maharashtra greenfield is still at land-acquisition stage without a clear plan.
